- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) or shows strong reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect sentiment shift.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next few days; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model shows high variance; use median of recent 5–7 day history as baseline.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-1.00” in last 3–5 days, model underperforms; add 2–3% to forecast to compensate.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid sharp downward trends unless sentiment is clearly bearish; if sentiment is neutral or positive, avoid predicting drops >3% from prior day.
